title: SWISA
abstract: This data provides daily continental estimates of the Soil Water Index (SWI), representing moisture conditions across different soil layers. SWI daily images are generated from the EUMETSAT ASCAT 25 km Surface Soil Moisture (SSM) product in orbit format and include a quality flag indicating the availability of SSM measurements used for SWI calculations. In addition to surface soil moisture, the SWI provides information on moisture conditions within the underlying soil profile, including the plant root zone, estimated using an infiltration model that combines surface soil moisture data with soil characteristics.

title: CYGNSS_L3_SOIL_MOISTURE_V3.2
abstract: The CYGNSS Level 3 Soil Moisture V3.2 dataset is provided by the CYGNSS Science Team of the University of Michigan. It estimates volumetric water content for soils between 0-5 cm depth at a 6-hour discretization for most of the subtropics from the V3.2 reflectivity measurements provided in the CYGNSS L1 SDR dataset (https://doi.org/10.5067/CYGNS-L1X32). CYGNSS was launched on 15 December 2016, it is a NASA Earth System Science Pathfinder Mission that was launched with the purpose of collecting the first frequent space?based measurements of surface wind speeds in the inner core of tropical cyclones. Originally made up of a constellation of eight micro-satellites, the observatories provide nearly gap-free Earth coverage using an orbital inclination of approximately 35° from the equator, with a mean (i.e., average) revisit time of seven hours and a median revisit time of three hours. The soil moisture retrieval algorithm is an update of the previous version developed by UCAR-CU using a linear regression of CYGNSS angle-normalized effective surface reflectivity trained against collocated SMAP soil moisture during the calibration period 8/1/2018 to 11/15/2023. The data are archived in daily files in netCDF-4 format. Volumetric soil moisture water content in units of cm3/cm3 is provided with two gridding resolutions, 9x9 km and 36x36 km. The variable SM_subdaily contains data reported in six hour intervals. The variable SM_daily provides a daily average. The time series covers the period from August 2018 to present.

title: LPRM_TMI_DY_SOILM3
abstract: The TMI/TRMM Surface Soil Moisture L3 1 day daytime V001 dataset is a Level 3 (gridded) product derived from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) Microwave Imager (TMI). It provides land surface parameters, including surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM). Each day produces two files: one daytime (ascending) and one nighttime (descending), stored as separate products. This document describes the daytime product. The dataset spans from December 1997 to April 2015, when the TRMM instruments ceased operation prior to satellite reentry. The LPRM applies a forward radiative transfer model to estimate surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth, while land surface temperature is separately derived from TMI?s Ka-band (37 GHz). This methodology is adaptable across microwave frequencies, supporting the use of passive microwave data from multiple satellites. Input data originate from the TMI Brightness Temperatures (1B-11) product, specifically from daytime passes, processed using LPRM (LPRM/TMI/TRMM L2, LPRM_TMI_SOILM2_V001).

title: LPRM_TMI_NT_SOILM3
abstract: The TMI/TRMM Surface Soil Moisture L3 1 day nighttime V001 dataset is a Level 3 (gridded) product derived from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) Microwave Imager (TMI). It provides land surface parameters, including surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM). Each day produces two files: one daytime (ascending) and one nighttime (descending), stored as separate products. This document describes the nighttime product. The dataset spans from December 1997 to April 2015, when the TRMM instruments ceased operation prior to satellite reentry. The LPRM applies a forward radiative transfer model to estimate surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth, while land surface temperature is separately derived from TMI?s Ka-band (37 GHz). A key feature of this methodology is its flexibility to operate at multiple microwave frequencies, enabling the exploitation of passive microwave data from diverse satellite missions. Input data originate from the TMI Brightness Temperatures (1B- 11) product, specifically from nighttime passes, processed using LPRM (LPRM/TMI/TRMM L2, LPRM_TMI_SOILM2_V001).

title: LPRM_TMI_SOILM2
abstract: The TMI/TRMM Surface Soil Moisture L2 (LPRM) dataset is a Level 2 swath product derived from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) Microwave Imager (TMI). It provides land surface parameters, including surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM). Each swath includes associated geolocation fields. The dataset spans from December 1997 to April 2015, ending when the TRMM instruments were deactivated prior to satellite reentry. The spatial resolution is approximately 45 km, corresponding to TMI?s X-band (10.7 GHz). Land surface temperature is independently derived from the Ka-band (37 GHz), while soil moisture and vegetation optical depth are estimated through a forward radiative transfer model. This methodology is adaptable to different microwave frequencies, enabling the use of passive microwave data from multiple satellites. Input data are sourced from the TMI Brightness Temperatures (1B-11) product, archived at the Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC).

title: LPRM_WINDSAT_DY_SOILM3
abstract: The WindSat/Coriolis Surface Soil Moisture L3 1-Day 25 km × 25 km Daytime V001 dataset is derived from observations by the WindSat polarimetric microwave radiometer aboard the Naval Research Laboratory?s Coriolis satellite. It provides daily gridded measurements of surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM) applied to WindSat brightness temperatures (sdrLowRes) from daytime passes. Land surface temperature is independently estimated from the Ka-band (37.0 GHz) channel, while surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth are obtained through a forward radiative transfer model. Each day includes separate ascending (daytime) and descending (nighttime) products, with this dataset representing the daytime passes. The temporal coverage spans from February 2003 to July 2012. Data are archived and distributed by the Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC).

title: ASCAT SSM CDR v5 12.5 km (H115)
abstract: This data provides a time series of Soil Moisture on a fixed Earth grid with 12.5 km sampling. It represents the water content of the 0?5 cm topsoil layer, expressed in degree of saturation from 0 to 100%. Seasonal vegetation effects are accounted for, and contributions from vegetation, land cover, and surface topography are minimized. The dataset covers the period 2007?2018 and represents a reprocessed record based on a consistent retrieval algorithm.

title: SM-DAS-DR2018-EXT (DATA RECORDS H140)
abstract: This data provides a reprocessed liquid soil moisture profile index for four different soil layers, covering the root zone from the surface to approximately 3 metres. It is generated by the offline ECMWF land surface data assimilation system at 24-hour time steps. The product offers a consistent time series over 2015?2016 of both surface and root zone soil moisture with daily global coverage, supporting hydrological applications and water budget investigations. It serves as an extension of the H27 product for the same period.

title: SSM ASCAT DR2017 EXT TS12.5 (H112)
abstract: This data provides a time series of surface soil moisture on a discrete global grid (DGG) with a spatial resolution of 25 km (grid spacing 12.5 km). The product represents the water content in the upper soil layer (< 2 cm) in relative units from completely dry (0%) to full water capacity (100%). Soil moisture is retrieved from radar backscatter observations measured by the ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer) instrument aboard the MetOp satellites. The temporal sampling is irregular (typically every 1?2 days) depending on latitude. Each soil moisture estimate includes an associated noise value to indicate uncertainty. This Interim Climate Data Record (ICDR) extends the previous product 10.15770/EUM_SAF_H_0004.

abstract: This data is a remote sensing product derived from the multi-angle backscatter observations of the Metop ASCAT instrument. title: Experimental Break-Adjusted COMBINED Product
abstract: This data provides the Soil Moisture CCI COMBINED break-adjusted dataset, produced as part of the European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture Essential Climate Variable (ECV) Climate Change Initiative (CCI) project. The break-adjusted product has been developed experimentally in version 07.1 to reduce temporal discontinuities in the merged soil moisture record by adjusting dataset statistics between merging periods, using ERA5 soil moisture as a reference (see Preimesberger et al., 2020). The COMBINED product merges Level 2 scatterometer (active microwave) and radiometer (passive microwave) soil moisture retrievals from the AMI-WS, ASCAT, SMMR, SSM/I, TMI, AMSR-E, WindSat, FY-3B, FY-3C, FY-3D, AMSR2, MIRAS (SMOS), GPM, and SMAP satellite instruments. PASSIVE and ACTIVE products have also been created within the CCI framework. The v07.1 COMBINED break-adjusted dataset is provided as global daily images in NetCDF-4 classic file format, with a spatial resolution of 0.25 degrees. It contains surface soil moisture expressed in volumetric units [m³/m³] and covers the period 1978-11-01 to 2021-12-31. The dataset is supported by documentation, including the Algorithm Theoretical Baseline Document and Preimesberger et al. (2020), which describe the methodology and adjustment process. Data were processed by the ESA CCI Soil Moisture project team and are distributed via the CEDA ESA CCI Open Data Portal.

abstract: This data is part of the European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture Climate Change Initiative (CCI) project and represents the Soil Moisture CCI ACTIVE dataset, one of three datasets produced (ACTIVE, PASSIVE, and COMBINED). The dataset was processed by the ESA CCI Soil Moisture project team and is available via the ESA CCI Open Data Portal and CEDA repository.

abstract: This data provides the Soil Moisture CCI COMBINED dataset, one of three datasets created as part of the European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture Essential Climate Variable (ECV) Climate Change Initiative (CCI) project. title: SPL2SMA
abstract: This dataset provides the Level-2 (L2) soil moisture product from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, launched in 2015. SMAP carries both an active radar and a passive L-band radiometer to measure soil moisture content and freeze/thaw state, supporting applications in weather forecasting, agriculture, water resource management, and climate studies. The L2 product delivers global land surface soil moisture estimates obtained from SMAP radar observations during 6:00 a.m. descending half-orbit passes, supplemented by ancillary data such as surface temperature and vegetation water content. The radar backscatter data used to derive soil moisture are resampled onto a 3 km, Earth-fixed, cylindrical Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) to ensure consistent spatial representation.

title: AE_Land
abstract: This Level-2B land surface product provides gridded estimates of surface soil moisture in the top 1 cm of soil, derived from the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer for EOS (AMSR-E) onboard the Aqua satellite. AMSR-E is a multichannel passive microwave instrument developed by the National Space Development Agency (NASDA) of Japan, and is a modified version of the AMSR instrument on ADEOS-II. Both instruments operate in polar, sun-synchronous orbits, with equator crossings at 10:30 a.m. (ADEOS-II) and 1:30 p.m. (Aqua). Soil moisture is estimated from AMSR-E/Aqua L2A brightness temperature (Tb) measurements using two algorithms: the Normalized Polarization Difference (NPD) algorithm and the Single Channel Algorithm (SCA). The product also provides ancillary information including vegetation and surface roughness, observation counts for various surface conditions, and quality assessment (QA) flags, which facilitate interpretation of the soil moisture retrievals.

title: AQ3_ANSM
abstract: The NASA Aquarius instrument was indeed part of the Satélite de Aplicaciones Científicas (SAC-D), which was a joint mission between NASA and Argentina's space agency, CONAE (Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales). The mission was launched on June 10, 2011. Aquarius was a passive microwave radiometer designed to measure global sea surface salinity. The primary goal of the Aquarius instrument was to map global sea surface salinity with a resolution of about 150 kilometers every 7 days, providing valuable data for understanding the Earth's water cycle and its relationship to ocean circulation, climate, and the water cycle. Aquarius utilized three passive microwave radiometers to measure microwave emissions from the Earth's surface, which were then used to derive the sea surface salinity. It operated at a frequency of 1.413 GHz. This data set contains Level-3 gridded annual global soil moisture estimates derived from the NASA Aquarius passive microwave radiometer on the SAC-D.

title: AQ3_DYSM
abstract: The NASA Aquarius/SAC-D Surface Soil Moisture L3 1 day dataset is a Level 3 (gridded) product derived from the Aquarius instrument aboard the SAC-D satellite, a joint mission between NASA and Argentina?s space agency, CONAE. Aquarius was a passive microwave radiometer designed primarily to measure global sea surface salinity, but its observations also support the retrieval of land surface parameters, including surface soil moisture. Each daily product provides global coverage, with input data processed to generate gridded soil moisture estimates. Aquarius operated at a frequency of 1.413 GHz and utilized passive microwave measurements to infer surface soil moisture. The retrieval approach applies microwave radiative transfer models to estimate soil moisture from brightness temperature observations. A key feature of this methodology is its applicability across different passive microwave frequencies, enabling integration with other satellite soil moisture products. Input data for this dataset originate from the Aquarius Level-2 brightness temperature products, which are processed to generate daily Level-3 gridded soil moisture (LPRM- based) estimates.

abstract: The NASA Aquarius instrument was indeed part of the Satélite de Aplicaciones Científicas (SAC-D), which was a joint mission between NASA and Argentina's space agency, CONAE (Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales). The mission was launched on June 10, 2011. Aquarius was a passive microwave radiometer designed to measure global sea surface salinity. The primary goal of the Aquarius instrument was to map global sea surface salinity with a resolution of about 150 kilometers every 7 days, providing valuable data for understanding the Earth's water cycle and its relationship to ocean circulation, climate, and the water cycle. Aquarius utilized three passive microwave radiometers to measure microwave emissions from the Earth's surface, which were then used to derive the sea surface salinity. It operated at a frequency of 1.413 GHz. This data set contains Level-3 gridded seasonal global soil moisture climatology estimates derived from the NASA Aquarius passive microwave radiometer on SAC-D.

abstract: The AMSR-E/Aqua Surface Soil Moisture L3 1-Day 25 km Ascending V002 dataset is derived from observations by the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer?EOS (AMSR-E) aboard NASA?s Aqua satellite. It provides daily gridded measurements of surface soil moisture, land surface temperature, and vegetation water content, retrieved using the Land Parameter Retrieval Model (LPRM) applied to AMSR-E resampled brightness temperatures (AE_L2A). title: NSIDC-0800
abstract: This data provides global estimates of soil moisture and vegetation optical depth (VOD) by combining observations from NASA?s Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP, launched in 2015) and ESA?s Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS, launched in 2009) missions. Two products are available: the SMOS-Based SMAP L2 Radiometer Half-Orbit 9 km Soil Moisture product (NSIDC-0799) and the SMAP/SMOS L3 Radiometer 9 km Soil Moisture product (NSIDC-0800). The L2 product is derived from half-orbit SMOS granules (6 AM ascending or 6 PM descending) after inter-calibration of brightness temperatures at a 40° incidence angle and retrieval of soil moisture and VOD using the SMAP Dual Channel Algorithm (DCA). The L3 product integrates one day?s worth of SMAP SPL2SMP_E data with SMOS-derived L2 data, providing combined ascending (6 PM/AM) and descending (6 AM/PM) retrievals in separate arrays. The data are provided on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) at 9 km spatial resolution in NetCDF format. SMAP and SMOS are both L-band satellites that measure brightness temperatures, soil moisture, and VOD approximately every 2?3 days with a spatial resolution of ~40 km. By merging their observations, this dataset reduces the revisit time to about one day, enhancing the monitoring of rapid hydrological processes such as groundwater recharge, soil drying after rainfall, and pre-storm soil moisture conditions important for runoff prediction.

title: SM_SCIE_AMS_CLA4ND
abstract: This dataset provides global surface soil moisture (SM) estimates derived from AMSR-E brightness temperature (Tb) observations using a neural network (NN) approach trained with Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) Level-3 soil moisture data as a reference. The goal of this approach is to produce a long-term soil moisture time series (2003?2011) with minimal bias and a similar dynamic range as the SMOS L3 SM product. The NN establishes a non-linear global relationship between AMSR-E Tb and SMOS SM during their 1.5- year concurrent period, allowing the reconstruction of soil moisture from earlier AMSR-E observations. Sensitivity analyses showed that AMSR-E Tb?s in H polarization at 23 and 36 GHz and V polarization at 36 GHz are optimal for retrieving soil temperature (Tsoil). For soil moisture, several combinations of input channels performed similarly, with a chosen NN using C and X bands plus Tsoil information to produce the final soil moisture estimates.

abstract: This data provides time series of surface soil moisture on a discrete global grid (DGG) with a spatial resolution of 25 km (grid spacing 12.5 km). The temporal sampling rate is irregular, with observations available every 1?2 days depending on latitude. Each surface soil moisture estimate includes an associated noise value, providing a measure of retrieval uncertainty.

title: WC_LSMEM_SOILM_025
abstract: The AMSR-E/Aqua Surface Soil Moisture L3 1-Day 0.25° × 0.25° V001 dataset is a global product derived from passive microwave brightness temperatures measured by the 10.65 and 36.5 GHz radiometers on the AMSR-E instrument aboard NASA?s Aqua satellite. Covering the period from 2002 to 2011, it provides estimates of surface soil moisture and vegetation optical depth generated using Princeton?s Land Surface Microwave Emission Model (LSMEM). The algorithm simultaneously solves radiative transfer equations for horizontally and vertically polarized brightness temperatures at 10.65 GHz, while land surface temperature is estimated from the 36.5 GHz vertically polarized channel using a regression relationship. The dataset excludes snow-covered regions and assumes constant atmospheric brightness temperatures, rendering atmospheric corrections unnecessary. Data are archived and distributed by the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC).

title: SMOS-IC
abstract: The Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission, launched by the European Space Agency (ESA) in 2009, provides global measurements of soil moisture over land and sea surface salinity over oceans. The mission operates the L-band Microwave Imaging Radiometer using Aperture Synthesis (MIRAS), which measures brightness temperatures at 1.4 GHz across multiple incidence angles. These observations improve climate and weather prediction, hydrological modeling, and the monitoring of Earth?s water and carbon cycles. The SMOS-INRA-CESBIO (SMOS-IC) soil moisture product was developed by INRA (Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique) and CESBIO (Centre d?Études Spatiales de la BIOsphère) to retrieve global soil moisture (SM) and L-band Vegetation Optical Depth (L-VOD). The algorithm is based on a simplified two- parameter inversion of the L-MEB model, designed to minimize dependence on auxiliary data and reduce uncertainties related to heterogeneous land cover, antenna patterns, and SMOS viewing geometry. The product is provided at 25 km spatial resolution on the Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0), in NetCDF format. SMOS-IC is a scientific dataset distributed by the CATDS but is not an operational product updated on a daily basis.

title: ASCAT25, OSI-102, OAS025
abstract: This data provides the ASCAT Multi-parameter product, which contains surface wind vectors over the ocean and a soil moisture index over land. The product also includes the backscatter values used in the retrieval of these parameters, together with several quality flags to support data interpretation. For numerical weather prediction (NWP) applications, the product is distributed in BUFR format, while the netCDF version contains wind data only. Users requiring ASCAT backscatter, wind, or soil moisture index data in other formats should refer to the dedicated product entries. Although the OSI SAF is identified as the originating centre, the soil moisture index processing is performed by EUMETSAT. For wind data prior to 1 April 2014, users are advised to use the reprocessed ASCAT wind data records (EO:EUM:DAT:METOP:OSI-150-A, EO:EUM:DAT:METOP:OSI-150-B) rather than this archived near-real-time product. Metop-A data are available in the Data Centre up to 15 November 2021.

title: SSM-ASCAT-NRT-DIS (H08)
abstract: This data is a disaggregated version of the global ASCAT near real-time (NRT) product (H16), originally generated at the EUMETSAT Headquarters and disseminated via EUMETCast. The disaggregation is performed using a pre-computed fine-mesh scaling layer derived from statistical analysis of C-band SAR imagery. A linear relationship between local (fine-scale) and regional (coarse-scale) backscatter information is established through multi-annual image analysis. The downscaling parameter database is then applied to disaggregate the scatterometer pixels to the fine mesh in near real-time. The SAR imagery used for generating this database comes from ENVISAT ASAR in ScanSAR Global Mode (years 2004?2012), with plans to incorporate imagery from Sentinel-1 in the future. The resulting disaggregated product, sampled at kilometer-scale resolution, allows better representation of local soil moisture patterns, making it more suitable for hydrological applications.

title: SWI
abstract: This data provides daily continental estimates of the Soil Water Index (SWI), representing moisture conditions across different soil layers. SWI daily images are generated from the EUMETSAT ASCAT 25 km Surface Soil Moisture (SSM) product in orbit format and include a quality flag indicating the availability of SSM measurements used for SWI calculations. In addition to surface soil moisture, the SWI provides information on moisture conditions within the underlying soil profile, including the plant root zone, estimated using an infiltration model that combines surface soil moisture data with soil characteristics.
